newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Analysts see poker game between KPN and BTA.
newsitem.headline: Analysts see poker game between KPN and BTA.

text.p: A poker game over the future of Australian transport firm TNT Ltd has started between 19.99 percent shareholder Bankers Trust Australia (BTA) and takeover bidder Koninklijke PTT Nederland NV, analysts say.

BTA on Wednesday cast doubts on the future of Dutch telecom and postal firm KPN's A$2.45 a share recommended offer for TNT when it said it was at the lower end of its valuations and declined to comment on whether it would accept the offer.
Whether KPN raises its offer for TNT, which has lucrative European businesses, could depend on who blinks first -- and analysts on Thursday were uncertain as to who that might be.
Some say KPN, applauded for its foray outside the Netherlands, could lose face if it drops the bid, others say the same would happen if it were seen to be paying too much for TNT.

"Analysts are concerned about the price being paid, they were thinking the price was generous. I think this is an aggressive move by BT but I suspect that it isn't going to force a higher price," said Chris Tucker of Paribas in London.
At A$2.45 a share, KPN's surprise 2.7 billion guilder bid last week valued TNT's shares at a 50 percent premium to their pre-bid closing.

"Our opinion is that the bid is fully valued, that was the opinion of a lot of transport analysts who advised to take the money and run," said Eric de Graaf at ING Barings. "In my view it looks like Bankers Trust is trying to get some extra money."

Analysts pointed out that the two parties are not yet in open conflict. "BT didn't say they didn't accept the bid, they just said they were thinking about it and that it was a bit low. It looks pretty speculative," said De Graaf.

"If you really think this company is cheap at 50 percent above the (pre-bid) market price then I think you should have bought the whole company," said another analyst, adding he believed BTA might still be prepared to accept the offer.
"That's the beauty of topping up (BTA's) stake. From that, you up the possibilities to get more money out of the whole holding. From that point of view they can't lose," he said.
Bankers Trust Australia (BTA) has increased its stake in TNT by 18.04 million shares to 117 million, since the bid was announced, paying less than the offer price.
The emergence of a second bidder could strengthen BTA's hand if it did decide to hold out, although analysts were not enthusiastic about the prospects.

"It's possible. I don't know who would really want it at more than A$2.45," said another analyst, adding speculation about a possible move from Federal Express Corp came back to the point that KPN's offer appeared to value TNT fully.

Joost van Beek at Van Meer James Capel believed it was unlikely that Bankers Trust Australia would aim to hold out on its own. "Maybe if a few other larger shareholders group together then of course I think KPN has no choice but to raise the bid if they want to go ahead," he said.
But he added: "I think KPN will stick to the $2.45 and just see how it goes and maybe expect finally BT to accept the offer. As far as we can judge the KPN bid certainly does not look low."
De Graaf said the position was difficult to gauge, but on balance KPN might grit its teeth and push on with its bid even if BTA did decide to hold back its shares.
"I think it's more possible that KPN would raise the bid rather than drop it," said De Graaf.

"If you say to the world that it's a perfect fit and not too expensive and that you're really happy with it and that you see a lot of potential and large synergy possibilities, then it's really difficult to say well we do want it but we don't want to pay a little bit extra," he said.

Others thought BTA might ultimately put its shares into KPN's offer. "I think BTA is flying a kite. The comments I've seen from other analysts of TNT seem to suggest that they think BTA is out of order on this," said one analyst. -- Keiron Henderson, Amsterdam Newsroom +31 20 504 5000
